canonical.title: Testing the waters: a staged, reversible path from a Windows dev workstation to Linux

children.title: The staged ladder: what each rung of a Windows→Linux move actually proves
children.summary: A rung-by-rung ladder from WSL2 to full switch, with what each rung proves, what it structurally hides, the go/no-go signal, and the cost of retreating.

children.title: WSL2 as rung zero — what it proves, and the exact wall it hits
children.summary: WSL2 retires every userland risk in a Linux migration and none of the machine-ownership risks; here is where the line falls in 2026.

children.title: Trial hardware and VM paths for evaluating Linux before you commit (2026)
children.summary: Live USB first (€10, 15 minutes, proves your actual hardware), then a full install on an external NVMe SSD (€90–150) — everything else is a detour.

children.title: Dual-boot Linux next to Windows in 2026 without wrecking the Windows install
children.summary: Buy a second NVMe, keep the two OSes ignorant of each other, and pick Linux from the firmware boot menu — the layout with the smallest blast radius on your Windows install.

children.title: Living in both OSes: running Windows and Linux for months without your setup rotting
children.summary: One source of truth per asset class, replicated by a tool that knows the OS difference — never a shared partition and never two hand-edited copies.

children.title: Dropbox on Linux and shared folders: what actually works in 2026
children.summary: The official Linux client now supports btrfs/zfs/xfs, but you cannot share one Dropbox folder between a Windows and a Linux install, and code repos do not belong in Dropbox at all.

children.title: Exit criteria and the blocker inventory: decide the Linux switch on evidence, not vibes
children.summary: A fill-in blocker inventory plus tickable go/no-go criteria and a pre-committed rollback date for a Windows-to-Linux workstation trial.

sources.title: Comparing WSL Versions — Microsoft Learn
sources.claim: WSL2 runs a real Linux kernel with systemd and full syscall compatibility, but uses NAT networking with a changing IP, has no serial-port support and needs usbipd for USB devices.

sources.claim: A live USB session does not alter your computer's configuration in any way.

sources.title: How to install Linux on an external SSD — gHacks

sources.claim: Changes to the NTFS partition table are a documented BitLocker recovery trigger.

sources.claim: The August 2024 SBAT update produced 'Verifying shim SBAT data failed: Security Policy Violation' on dual-boot machines.

sources.title: Dual boot with Windows — ArchWiki
sources.claim: There is only one ESP per drive; hibernating one OS and booting the other requires two ESPs on two physical disks.

sources.title: anishathalye/git-remote-dropbox
sources.claim: Concurrent changes to a git repository inside a sync folder can result in a corrupted Git repository.

sources.title: Dropbox system requirements
sources.claim: Dropbox on Linux officially supports ext4, zfs, eCryptFS (backed by ext4), xfs and btrfs for the folder holding the Dropbox directory.

sources.title: Delete and restore files — Dropbox Help
sources.claim: Deleting a file inside a shared folder removes it from the shared folder for everyone.

sources.title: Sharing a Dropbox folder between Windows and Linux installs — Dropbox Community
sources.claim: One on-disk Dropbox folder cannot be shared between a Windows and a Linux install on the same PC.

sources.title: WSL is great, but run Linux natively instead — XDA
sources.claim: Anything involving kernel modules, low-level system configuration or hardware access is limited or outright blocked in WSL2.

sources.title: Portable Linux on an SSD — dspdev.io
sources.claim: The idea with running Linux on a separate disk is the ability to basically press delete, and the Linux system is gone.

sources.title: Installing Ubuntu on an external portable SSD, and pitfalls — Geek Culture
sources.claim: Installers can write the bootloader to the internal ESP; disabling internal drives in UEFI before installing prevents it.

sources.title: Should I switch from Windows to Linux? — AnandTech Forums
sources.claim: Practitioners converge on VM-then-spare-machine, live-USB hardware checks, and eventually wiping the Windows drive.

sources.title: Live USB persistence and kernel updates — EndeavourOS Forum
sources.claim: Persistent live media chokes on initramfs and kernel updates, so proprietary NVIDIA modules cannot be tested there.

sources.title: PCI passthrough via OVMF — ArchWiki
sources.claim: GPU passthrough requires a second GPU dedicated to the guest and cooperative IOMMU grouping.

sources.title: WPF and WinForms on macOS and Linux — Microsoft Q&A
sources.claim: WPF and WinForms designers have no Linux port and Microsoft has announced none.

sources.title: 30 days of Linux vs Windows — WindowsPost
sources.claim: Days 1-3 are smooth, week 1 is the trough, and by week two the friction drops off.

sources.title: The year of the Linux desktop — Xe Iaso

sources.claim: 835 points and 639 comments; a sanity check on how contested the switch still is.
